Beside it, the rule: facing up means add, a positive number steps forwards and a negative number steps backwards; the adding and the backwards lines are highlighted. It lands on minus 12: minus 4 plus minus 4 plus minus 4, so 3 times minus 4 equals minus 12.

pages.name: Two lots of −5
pages.why: 2 × −5 is two lots of −5, added together. Each −5 steps the marker 5 backwards, from 0 to −5, then on to −10. So 2 × −5 = −10.

pages.task: Carry the pattern on. What is −1 × −4?
pages.why: Each row so far has one lot of −4 fewer, so the answer climbs 4. Carry that climb on: after 0 × −4 = 0, which is neither positive nor negative, comes −1 × −4 = 4.

pages.name: Turn it
pages.task: Work out −3 × −4 by turning. Start from 3 × 4 = 12, and give it one half-turn for each minus sign.
pages.why: −3 is 3 × −1 and −4 is 4 × −1, so each minus sign brings one half-turn. Two half-turns take 12 round and back, so −3 × −4 = 12. Same signs give a positive answer.

pages.name: Adding is different
pages.why: Adding −4 steps the marker 4 backwards, from −3 down to −7. Half-turns come from multiplying, so −3 × −4 = 12 but −3 + (−4) = −7.

pages.name: A tank
pages.task: Say a tank's level changes by −0.4 m each hour. What is the change over 3 hours?
pages.why: Each hour adds −0.4 m to the change, so 3 hours give 3 × −0.4 = −1.2. The level ends 1.2 m lower than it started.

pages.name: Which is 15?
pages.why: −5 × −3 has two minus signs, so two half-turns bring 15 back to 15. −5 × 3 has one, so it is −15. −5 + (−3) adds, so it is −8.
